change.title: pr-37634
change.description:
Encoding context to access token IDs closes #37118
Shorter encoding of access token
change.author: mposolda

findings.title: isAccessTokenId never checks the grant shortcut: wrong offset and inverted comparison
findings.body: The encoded prefix is `<session 2><tokenType 2><grant 2>` (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:78-81), so the grant shortcut is `substring(4, 6)`. `substring(3, 5)` reads the last char of the token type and the first char of the grant (e.g. `onrtac` → `ta`). The check is also inverted: it returns `false` when the slice *equals* the expected shortcut. Together this means the matcher accepts any token id of the form `xxxxxx:<uuid>`, whatever grant is encoded. So `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` assert nothing about the grant. If you only fix the offset, every one of these assertions fails, because the inverted check is still there. Fix: `if (items[0].length() != 6 || !items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. The length check also stops an id with a short prefix from throwing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning a mismatch.

findings.title: rawTokenId null check validates grantType instead
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` a second time. A null `rawTokenId` gets through, and `encodeTokenId` then produces `xxxxxx:null` with no error. Change the argument to `rawTokenId`.

findings.title: client_credentials, UMA and legacy token-exchange tokens are encoded with grant 'na'
findings.body: The grant type reaches the encoder only through the `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` attribute on the client session context (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:57-60). ClientCredentialsGrantType builds its token with `tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken()` (ClientCredentialsGrantType.java:140-141) and never goes through `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse`, so the attribute is never set. Every service-account token is therefore encoded as `..na:<id>`, even though this factory registers `cc` and the unit test's sample id is `trltcc:1234`. The same applies to the UMA permission grant (`pg`, AuthorizationTokenService.java:358) and the legacy token-exchange path (AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:410): neither sets the attribute. Anything that reads the grant back from the jti gets a wrong answer with no error. Set `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())` before `generateAccessToken()` in ClientCredentialsGrantType, the same way ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.java:134 does, and do the same for the other two paths.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant factories
findings.body: Any deployed custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` stops compiling, or throws AbstractMethodError at runtime, the first time `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls `getShortcut()`. If a custom factory returns null, `ConcurrentHashMap.put` throws an NPE and startup fails. Consider a default method, or skipping and logging factories that have no shortcut. Tokens from such grants could then fall back to `na`.

findings.title: Grant-type attribute set twice on the password grant path
findings.body: This line sets `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` to `context.getGrantType()`. If this grant also goes through `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` (line 109), that sets the same value again. If it only uses `responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken()` (line 139), then this line is the one that matters and the call in the base class is not enough on its own. Either way, set it in one shared place, for example once the context is in hand, so grant paths like client_credentials do not each have to remember it.

contracts.action: initToken now asks TokenContextEncoderProvider to build the jti from the client session context
contracts.before_after: The grant type comes from the GRANT_TYPE attribute, which is set only by OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, ROPC, PreAuthorizedCode, refreshAccessToken and StandardTokenExchangeProvider. ClientCredentialsGrantType, AuthorizationTokenService and AbstractTokenExchangeProvider call generateAccessToken without setting it.
contracts.visible_effect: The jti in tokens and the TOKEN_ID in events now has a 6-char prefix; for client_credentials, UMA and legacy exchange the grant is 'na'.
contracts.failure_mode: encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException if the grant attribute holds a value with no registered shortcut; the token request then fails.

contracts.action: Encoder calls AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken to decide the token type
contracts.before_after: Mappers call it after initToken; the encoder now calls it during initToken. UseLightweightAccessTokenExecutor sets the session attribute on the TOKEN_REQUEST and other request events, which fire before the token is built.
contracts.failure_mode: NPE if session.getContext().getClient() is null, e.g. on the admin PolicyEvaluationService or KeycloakIdentity paths; I did not confirm that the client is set there.
contracts.open_question: Is the context client always set before createClientAccessToken on the admin policy-evaluation and KeycloakIdentity paths?

contracts.action: Removal of the OAuth2GrantType.Context copy constructor; grantType read from formParams in the main constructor
contracts.before_after: No in-repo callers of the copy constructor. setFormParams does not refresh grantType.

summary: The PR encodes session type, token type and grant into the access token's jti. Three things need fixing. (1) Client_credentials, UMA and legacy token-exchange tokens never set the grant-type attribute, so they are encoded as 'na'. (2) The rawTokenId null check in AccessTokenContext checks grantType instead. (3) The AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher uses the wrong offset and an inverted comparison, so it never verifies the grant. Also worth considering: the new abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant factories.
